title.en: Volume 467 Biographies 254: Li Bingheng, Wang Tingxiang, Nie Shicheng, Luo Rongguang, Shou Shan Zu Sun : Rui Chang, Feng Xiang, Chong Yu
title.raw: 卷467 列傳二百五十四 李秉衡 王廷相 聂士成 罗荣光 寿山族孙：瑞昌 凤翔 崇玉

sentences.zh: 列傳二百五十四

translations.literal: Biographies 254
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 254

sentences.zh: 李秉衡王廷相聶士成羅榮光壽山族孫瑞昌鳳翔崇玉等

translations.literal: Li Bingheng, Wang Tingxiang, Nie Shicheng, Luo Rongguang, Shou Shan clan grandsons Rui Chang, Feng Xiang, Chong Yu, and others
translations.idiomatic: Li Bingheng, Wang Tingxiang, Nie Shicheng, Luo Rongguang, and the Shou Shan clan grandsons Rui Chang, Feng Xiang, Chong Yu, among others

sentences.zh: 李秉衡，字鑑堂，奉天海城人。

translations.literal: Li Bingheng, styled Jiantang, was a man of Haicheng in Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bingheng, whose style was Jiantang, came from Haicheng in Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 初入貲為縣丞，遷知縣。

translations.literal: At first he entered office by purchase as assistant magistrate, and was transferred to county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: He first bought his way in as an assistant magistrate, then was promoted to county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 光緒五年，除知冀州。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Guangxu, he was appointed magistrate of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1879 he was appointed magistrate of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，發倉粟，不給。

translations.literal: That year there was famine; he opened the granary grain, but it was not enough.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck that year, he opened the government granaries, but the stores were insufficient.

sentences.zh: 州俗重紡織，布賤，為醵金求遠遷，易糧歸，而裁其價以招民，民獲甦。

translations.literal: The prefecture's custom valued spinning and weaving; cloth was cheap; he pooled funds to seek distant transport, exchanged for grain and returned, and cut the price to attract the people; the people obtained revival.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the prefecture were devoted to weaving, but cloth sold cheaply. He raised funds to send it to distant markets, traded the proceeds for grain, and sold the grain at reduced prices to draw buyers; the populace thus recovered.

sentences.zh: 越二年，擢知永平府。

translations.literal: After two years, he was promoted to prefect of Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he was promoted to prefect of Yongping.

sentences.zh: 部議追論劫案，貶秩。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated on retrospectively prosecuting a robbery case and reduced his rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Board of Civil Appointments reviewed an old robbery case against him and lowered his rank.

sentences.zh: 李鴻章上其理狀，請免議，不獲。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang submitted his statement of reasoning and requested exemption from deliberation; it was not obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang submitted a memorial explaining the circumstances and asked that the case be dropped, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 時稱「北直廉吏第一」。

translations.literal: At the time he was called "the foremost honest official of North Zhili."
translations.idiomatic: He was then known as "the foremost honest official in Zhili."

sentences.zh: 以張之洞薦，超授浙江按察使，未到官，移廣西。

translations.literal: On Zhang Zhidong's recommendation, he was promoted beyond normal procedure to Zhejiang provincial judicial commissioner; before reaching office he was transferred to Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: On Zhang Zhidong's recommendation he was promoted out of turn to judicial commissioner of Zhejiang, but before he could take up the post he was transferred to Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 十年，平峒寨亂，晉二品秩。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he pacified the Dongzhai rebellion and was promoted to second-rank rank.
translations.idiomatic: In 1884 he pacified the Dongzhai uprising and was raised to the second rank.

sentences.zh: 明年，法人假越事寇邊，秉衡主龍州西運局。

translations.literal: The next year, the French used the Vietnam affair to raid the border; Bingheng headed the Longzhou Western Transport Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when the French used the Vietnamese crisis as a pretext to attack the border, Bingheng took charge of the Longzhou Western Transport Bureau.

sentences.zh: 是時財匱，戰士不得餉，蹂屍輿廝，無人過問。

translations.literal: At that time finances were exhausted; warriors received no pay; bodies trampled carts and servants; no one inquired.
translations.idiomatic: Funds were exhausted; soldiers went unpaid, and corpses littered the roads while no one took notice.

sentences.zh: 秉衡益節儉，汰浮費，無分主客軍，給糧不絕，戰卹功賞力從厚。

translations.literal: Bingheng became still more frugal, eliminated wasteful expenses, made no distinction between host and guest armies in issuing grain without interruption, and in battle consolation and merit rewards were generously followed.
translations.idiomatic: Bingheng practiced still greater frugality, cut wasteful spending, issued rations without distinction between native and auxiliary troops, and rewarded battlefield merit generously.

sentences.zh: 复創設醫局，治負傷軍士，身自拊循之，日數四，雖末弁，亦延見，殷殷勗以殺敵報國。

translations.literal: He also newly established a medical bureau to treat wounded soldiers, personally comforted them four times a day, and even junior lieutenants were received and earnestly exhorted to kill the enemy and repay the state.
translations.idiomatic: He also founded a field hospital for wounded soldiers, visiting them in person four times a day. Even the lowest lieutenants were granted audiences and earnestly urged to kill the enemy in service of the state.

sentences.zh: 護撫命下，驩聲若雷動。

translations.literal: When the acting governor order came down, cheers were like thunder rolling.
translations.idiomatic: When the order appointing him acting governor arrived, cheers rang out like thunder.

sentences.zh: 與馮子材分任戰守。

translations.literal: He and Feng Zicai divided responsibility for battle and defense.
translations.idiomatic: He and Feng Zicai divided the duties of attack and defense between them.

sentences.zh: 諒山之捷，彭玉麟等疏言：「兩臣忠直，同得民心，亦同功最盛。

translations.literal: After the victory at Liangshan, Peng Yulin and others memorialized: "The two ministers are loyal and upright, equally won the people's hearts, and their achievements were equally greatest."
translations.idiomatic: After the victory at Liangshan, Peng Yulin and others memorialized: "These two ministers are loyal and upright, equally beloved by the people, and their achievements are equally outstanding."

sentences.zh: 」予優敘。

translations.literal: They were granted preferential commendation.
translations.idiomatic: They were granted preferential commendation.

sentences.zh: 重申前命為護撫，整營製，舉賢能，資遣越南游眾，越事漸告寧。

translations.literal: His former appointment as acting governor was reaffirmed; he reorganized camp regulations, promoted the worthy and capable, provided funds to repatriate Vietnamese stragglers, and the Vietnam affair gradually announced peace.
translations.idiomatic: His earlier appointment as acting governor was confirmed. He reorganized the camps, promoted capable men, funded the repatriation of Vietnamese stragglers, and the Vietnamese crisis gradually subsided.

sentences.zh: 新任巡撫沈秉成蒞官，乃乞病去。

translations.literal: When the new governor Shen Bingcheng took office, he then begged leave on grounds of illness and departed.
translations.idiomatic: When the new governor Shen Bingcheng assumed office, he requested leave on grounds of illness and retired.

sentences.zh: 二十年，東事棘，召為山東巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, eastern affairs were critical; he was summoned as Shandong governor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1894, as the crisis in the east sharpened, he was summoned to serve as governor of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 至則嚴紀律，杜苞苴。

translations.literal: On arrival he strictly enforced discipline and shut out bribery.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he enforced strict discipline and shut the door to bribery.

sentences.zh: 以威海、旅順筦鑰北門，遂率師駐煙台。

translations.literal: Because Weihai and Lüshun held the keys to the northern gate, he then led his army to garrison at Yantai.
translations.idiomatic: Since Weihai and Lüshun guarded the northern approaches, he led his troops to garrison Yantai.

sentences.zh: 聞旅順不守，劾罷丁汝昌、龔照嶼等，以警威海守將。

translations.literal: On hearing that Lüshun was not held, he impeached and removed Ding Ruchang, Gong Zhaoyu, and others to warn the Weihai defenders.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that Lüshun had fallen, he impeached and dismissed Ding Ruchang, Gong Zhaoyu, and others to warn the defenders at Weihai.

sentences.zh: 既而日軍浮三艦窺登州，秉衡悉萃精兵於西北，而榮城以戎備寡，為日軍所誘而獲，時論詬之。

translations.literal: Then the Japanese navy floated three ships to probe Dengzhou; Bingheng concentrated all elite troops in the northwest, but Rongcheng, with thin military preparations, was lured and taken by the Japanese; contemporary opinion reviled him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward three Japanese warships appeared off Dengzhou. Bingheng massed his best troops in the northwest, but Rongcheng, thinly defended, was lured into a trap and captured by the Japanese, and public opinion turned against him.

sentences.zh: 其時大刀會起，主仇教，勢漸張。

translations.literal: At that time the Dadao Society arose, devoted to anti-Christianity, and its power gradually spread.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Dadao Society arose, preaching hatred of Christianity, and its influence steadily grew.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，會眾戕德國教士，德使海靖要褫秉衡職，編修王廷相力爭之，徙督四川。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, the society massacred a German missionary; the German minister Haijing demanded stripping Bingheng of office; Hanlin compiler Wang Tingxiang argued fiercely; he was transferred to govern Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1897 members of the society killed a German missionary. The German minister von Heyking demanded Bingheng's dismissal; Hanlin compiler Wang Tingxiang argued strenuously on his behalf, and Bingheng was transferred to be governor of Sichuan instead.

sentences.zh: 海靖請益堅，乃罷免。

translations.literal: Haijing's demand grew still more insistent, and he was finally dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When von Heyking pressed his demand still harder, Bingheng was dismissed outright.

sentences.zh: 於是秉衡隱安陽，居三年，剛毅入樞廷，薦之起，入都。

translations.literal: Thereupon Bingheng retired in seclusion at Anyang for three years; when Gangyi entered the Grand Council he recommended him for recall and he entered the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Bingheng then lived in retirement at Anyang for three years. When Gangyi joined the Grand Council he recommended Bingheng for recall, and Bingheng came to the capital.

sentences.zh: 廷相慕其名，往訪，遂訂交。

translations.literal: Tingxiang admired his reputation, went to call on him, and they formed a friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Tingxiang admired his reputation, called on him, and the two became close friends.

sentences.zh: 朝命秉衡詣奉天按事，奏廷相自隨。

translations.literal: The court ordered Bingheng to proceed to Fengtian to investigate affairs; he memorialized to have Tingxiang accompany him of his own accord.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Bingheng to Fengtian to conduct an investigation; he memorialized asking that Tingxiang accompany him.

sentences.zh: 既至，糾不職者數人，皆廷相微服所詗知者。

translations.literal: On arrival, he censured several derelict officials, all of whom Tingxiang had learned of in plain clothes through inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he censured several negligent officials, every one of whom Tingxiang had identified through inquiries made in disguise.

sentences.zh: 還，會御史彭述疏請整飭長江水師，詔使秉衡往，秉衡固辭，太后責勉之，遂行。

translations.literal: On return, when censor Peng Shu memorialized requesting rectification of the Yangtze flotilla, an edict sent Bingheng there; Bingheng firmly declined; the Empress Dowager reproached and urged him, and he then went.
translations.idiomatic: On his return, when Censor Peng Shu memorialized calling for reform of the Yangtze flotilla, an edict dispatched Bingheng to carry it out. Bingheng firmly declined, but the Empress Dowager rebuked and urged him on, and he set out.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，拳禍作，枋事者矯詔趣戰，電各省，諸疆臣失措，商之鴻章。

translations.literal: After more than a year, the Boxer calamity arose; those handling affairs forged edicts urging battle and telegraphed the provinces; provincial governors were at a loss and consulted Li Hongzhang.
translations.idiomatic: A year later the Boxer crisis erupted. Those in charge forged edicts urging war and telegraphed the provinces. The governors were at a loss and turned to Li Hongzhang for counsel.

sentences.zh: 於是定畫保東南約，秉衡與焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon the plan to preserve the southeast was settled; Bingheng participated in it.
translations.idiomatic: The plan to shield the southeast was then agreed upon, and Bingheng took part in it.

sentences.zh: 無何，又請募師入衛。

translations.literal: Before long they again requested raising troops to enter and guard.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they again called for raising troops to defend the capital.

sentences.zh: 至京，入覲太后，力主戰，遂命統張春發、陳澤霖、夏辛酉、萬本華四軍，出屯楊村、河西塢。

translations.literal: On reaching Beijing he had audience with the Empress Dowager, strongly urged war, and was then ordered to command the four armies of Zhang Chunfa, Chen Zelin, Xia Xinyou, and Wan Benhua, going out to encamp at Yangcun and Hexiwu.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Beijing he had audience with the Empress Dowager and strongly urged war. He was then ordered to command the four armies of Zhang Chunfa, Chen Zelin, Xia Xinyou, and Wan Benhua, and encamped at Yangcun and Hexiwu.

sentences.zh: 戰才合，張、萬二軍先潰，澤霖自武清移壁，聞砲聲，軍皆走。

translations.literal: As soon as battle joined, Zhang's and Wan's two armies broke first; Zelin moved camp from Wuqing, and on hearing cannon fire the troops all fled.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as battle was joined, Zhang's and Wan's forces broke first. Zelin had moved camp from Wuqing, but at the sound of cannon fire his men too fled.

sentences.zh: 秉衡不得已，退通州，疾書致各將領，述諸軍畏葸狀，飲金死。

translations.literal: Bingheng had no choice but to withdraw to Tongzhou; he wrote urgently to the generals describing the troops' cowardice, then drank gold and died.
translations.idiomatic: Bingheng had no choice but to withdraw to Tongzhou. He wrote urgently to the generals describing the troops' cowardice, then took poison and died.

sentences.zh: 事聞，優詔賜卹，諡忠節。

translations.literal: When news arrived, a generous edict granted mourning stipends and posthumous title Zhongjie.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, an edict granted generous mourning stipends and the posthumous title Zhongjie (Loyal and Steadfast).

sentences.zh: 聯軍索罪魁，請重治，以先死免議，詔褫職，奪卹典。

translations.literal: The allied armies demanded the chief culprits and requested severe punishment; because he had died first he was exempted from deliberation, but an edict stripped his post and revoked mourning honors.
translations.idiomatic: The allied powers demanded the chief culprits and called for severe punishment. Because he had already died, he escaped formal prosecution, but an edict stripped his rank and revoked his mourning honors.

sentences.zh: 廷相，字梅岑，直隸承德人，本籍山東。

translations.literal: Tingxiang, styled Meicen, was a native of Chengde in Zhili with ancestral registration in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tingxiang, whose style was Meicen, was a native of Chengde in Zhili, though his family register was in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 少劬學，以孝稱。

translations.literal: In youth he studied diligently and was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied diligently and was known for his filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 光緒十三年進士，以編修督山西學政。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Guangxu he passed the jinshi examination; as Hanlin compiler he supervised Shanxi educational administration.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in 1887 and, as a Hanlin compiler, was appointed educational commissioner of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 口外七廳洊飢，有司匿不聞，為上流民殘弊狀，獲賑如腹地。

translations.literal: The seven districts beyond the passes suffered repeated famine; local officials concealed it and did not report; he memorialized upstream the people's wretched condition and obtained relief like the interior.
translations.idiomatic: The seven districts beyond the passes suffered repeated famine, which local officials concealed. He memorialized the court on the people's plight and secured relief on the same terms as the interior provinces.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，轉御史，敢言事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was transferred to censor and dared to speak on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1897 he was transferred to the Censorate and proved fearless in memorializing.

sentences.zh: 時宗室、覺羅官學久廢不葺，廷相謂培材宜自近始，請依八旗官學新章，求實際，議行。

translations.literal: At the time the imperial clan and Aisin Gioro official schools had long lain in disrepair; Tingxiang said cultivating talent should begin with those near at hand and requested following the new regulations of the Eight Banners official schools, seeking practical results; the proposal was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The schools for imperial clansmen and Aisin Gioro bannermen had long fallen into neglect. Tingxiang argued that cultivating talent should begin close to home and asked that the new regulations for the Eight Banners schools be applied in earnest; the proposal was adopted.

sentences.zh: 國用患不足，計臣議加賦，廷相力申李鴻藻議，為民請命，事遂寢。

translations.literal: State revenue feared insufficiency; planning officials proposed increasing levies; Tingxiang strongly upheld Li Hongzao's proposal, pleaded for the people, and the matter was then shelved.
translations.idiomatic: When state revenues ran short and fiscal planners proposed new taxes, Tingxiang strongly supported Li Hongzao's opposition and pleaded on behalf of the people; the proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 二十四年元旦，日食，疏請勤修省，條上七事，而尤以進賢退不肖為國家治亂之源。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day of the twenty-fourth year there was a solar eclipse; he memorialized requesting diligent self-cultivation and restraint, listing seven items, and especially took promoting the worthy and removing the unworthy as the source of a state's order and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of 1898 a solar eclipse occurred. He memorialized urging the throne to practice self-restraint, setting forth seven recommendations, and above all identifying the promotion of worthy men and removal of the unworthy as the root of national order and disorder.

sentences.zh: 因劾張廕桓媚外人、交近侍，並以浙江學政徐致祥秩滿調安徽，外似優隆，內實屏絕。

translations.literal: He thereby impeached Zhang Yin-huan for fawning on foreigners and associating with palace attendants, and also noted that Zhejiang educational commissioner Xu Zhixiang, on completing his term, was transferred to Anhui—outwardly seeming preferential promotion, inwardly in fact screening him off.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Zhang Yin-huan for currying favor with foreigners and consorting with palace eunuchs, and pointed out that when Xu Zhixiang completed his term as Zhejiang educational commissioner he was transferred to Anhui—a move that looked like promotion but was in fact banishment.

sentences.zh: 嚴旨下吏議，敕還原衙門行走。

translations.literal: A stern edict sent the matter to official deliberation, then ordered him to return to his original yamen and resume duties.
translations.idiomatic: A stern edict referred the matter to the Board of Punishments, then ordered him back to his original post.

sentences.zh: 拳亂起，秉衡出禦聯軍，廷相從。

translations.literal: When the Boxer turmoil arose, Bingheng went out to resist the allied armies and Tingxiang followed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Boxer uprising broke out, Bingheng went out to face the allied armies, and Tingxiang accompanied him.

sentences.zh: 及敗，尋秉衡不遇，還至倉頭橋，赴河死。

translations.literal: When they were defeated, he sought Bingheng but did not find him; returning to Cangtou Bridge, he went into the river and died.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat he searched for Bingheng without success. Returning to Cangtou Bridge, he threw himself into the river and drowned.

sentences.zh: 子履豐，拯之不及，從之，遇救免。

translations.literal: His son Lüfeng could not save him in time, followed him, and was rescued and spared.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lüfeng could not reach him in time, jumped in after him, and was rescued.

sentences.zh: 贈五品卿，予世職，賞履豐主事。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted fifth-rank chamberlain, given a hereditary office, and Lüfeng was rewarded with a secretary post.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the rank of fifth-grade chamberlain with a hereditary office, and his son Lüfeng was appointed a secretary.

sentences.zh: 聶士成，字功亭，安徽合肥人。

translations.literal: Nie Shicheng, styled Gongting, was a man of Hefei in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Nie Shicheng, whose style was Gongting, came from Hefei in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 初從袁甲三軍討捻，補把總。

translations.literal: At first he followed Yuan Jiasan's army to suppress the Nian and was appointed platoon commander.
translations.idiomatic: He first served under Yuan Jiasan in the campaign against the Nian rebels and was appointed platoon commander.

sentences.zh: 同治初，改隸淮軍，從劉銘傳分援江、浙、閩、皖，累遷至副將。

translations.literal: In the early Tongzhi period he was transferred to the Huai Army, followed Liu Mingchuan in separate relief of Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, and Anhui, and was repeatedly promoted to deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Tongzhi era he joined the Huai Army and served under Liu Mingchuan in campaigns across Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, and Anhui, rising eventually to deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 東捻敗，賜號力勇巴圖魯，擢總兵。

translations.literal: When the eastern Nian were defeated, he was granted the title Liyong Batulu and promoted to regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: After the eastern Nian were defeated he was granted the title Liyong Batulu and promoted to regional commander.

sentences.zh: 西捻平，晉提督。

translations.literal: When the western Nian were pacified, he was promoted to provincial commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When the western Nian were pacified he was promoted to provincial military governor.

sentences.zh: 光緒十年，法人據基隆，率師渡台灣，屢戰卻敵。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Guangxu the French occupied Keelung; he led his army across to Taiwan and repeatedly fought off the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In 1884, when the French seized Keelung, he led his troops to Taiwan and repeatedly repelled the enemy.

sentences.zh: 還北洋，統慶軍駐旅順。

translations.literal: He returned to the Northern Seas, commanded the Qing Army, and garrisoned Lüshun.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the Beiyang command, took charge of the Qing Army, and garrisoned Lüshun.

sentences.zh: 十七年，海軍大閱禮成，晉頭品秩。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, when the grand naval review ceremony was completed, he was promoted to first-rank rank.
translations.idiomatic: In 1891, after the grand naval review, he was raised to the first rank.

sentences.zh: 調統蘆臺淮、練諸軍，擊熱河朝陽教匪，擒斬其酋楊悅春，賞黃馬褂，易勇號曰巴圖隆阿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to command the Huai and trained troops at Lutai, attacked the Chaoyang sect rebels in Rehe, captured and beheaded their chieftain Yang Yuechun, was rewarded with the yellow riding jacket, and his brave title was changed to Batulong'a.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned to command the Huai and militia forces at Lutai, attacked the sect rebels at Chaoyang in Rehe, captured and executed their leader Yang Yuechun, was awarded the yellow riding jacket, and his martial title was changed to Batulong'a.

sentences.zh: 明年，授山西太原鎮總兵，仍留蘆臺治軍。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed regional commander of Taiyuan Garrison in Shanxi, but still remained at Lutai to manage the army.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed commander of the Taiyuan garrison in Shanxi but continued to manage his troops at Lutai.

sentences.zh: 請單騎巡邊，歷東三省俄羅斯東境、朝鮮八道，圖其山川阨塞，著東遊紀程。

translations.literal: He requested to patrol the border alone on horseback, traversing the three eastern provinces, Russia's eastern borderlands, and Korea's eight provinces, mapping their mountains, rivers, and strategic passes, and wrote An Account of an Eastern Journey.
translations.idiomatic: He asked permission to tour the frontier alone, traveling through the three eastern provinces, Russia's Maritime Province, and all eight Korean provinces, mapping terrain and strategic passes, and published An Account of an Eastern Journey.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，日韓亂起，隨提督葉志超軍牙山。

translations.literal: After a year, the Japan-Korea turmoil arose; he followed Provincial Commander Ye Zhichao's army to Asan.
translations.idiomatic: A year later, when war broke out between Japan and Korea, he accompanied Provincial Commander Ye Zhichao to Asan.

sentences.zh: 聞高升兵艦毀，語志超曰：「海道梗，牙山不可守。

translations.literal: On hearing that the transport Kowshing had been destroyed, he said to Zhichao: "The sea route is blocked; Asan cannot be held."
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that the transport Kowshing had been sunk, he told Zhichao, "The sea lanes are cut; Asan cannot be held."

sentences.zh: 公州背山面江，勢便利。

translations.literal: Gongju backs on mountains and faces the river; the terrain is advantageous.
translations.idiomatic: Gongju lies with mountains at its back and the river before it—a far more favorable position.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " Zhichao followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Zhichao agreed.

sentences.zh: 士成乃先諸軍發，次成歡，遇伏，迷失道，吏士無人色。

translations.literal: Shicheng then set out before the other armies, reached Seonghwan, encountered an ambush, lost the road, and officers and soldiers lost all color.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng marched ahead of the main force toward Seonghwan, ran into an ambush, and lost the road; officers and men turned pale with fear.

sentences.zh: 士成見二鶴立岡阜，語眾曰：「彼處無隱兵也！

translations.literal: Shicheng saw two cranes standing on a hillock and said to the crowd: "There are no hidden troops there!"
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng noticed two cranes standing on a hill and told his men, "There can be no ambush where cranes stand so calmly!"

sentences.zh: 」遂出險，往就志超。

translations.literal: " They then escaped danger and went to join Zhichao.
translations.idiomatic: They broke through the danger zone and rejoined Zhichao.

sentences.zh: 志超已棄公州行，追及之。

translations.literal: Zhichao had already abandoned Gongju and departed; Shicheng overtook him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhichao had already abandoned Gongju and fled; Shicheng caught up with him.

sentences.zh: 士成議趨平壤合大軍，而鴻章檄令內渡，以故平壤陷，得免議。

translations.literal: Shicheng proposed hurrying to Pyongyang to join the main army, but Hongzhang's dispatch ordered crossing back inland; because of this Pyongyang fell, and he was exempted from deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng urged marching on Pyongyang to join the main force, but Li Hongzhang ordered a withdrawal across the sea. Pyongyang therefore fell, yet Shicheng escaped censure because he had obeyed orders.

sentences.zh: 志超逮問，宋慶接統諸軍，遣士成守虎山。

translations.literal: Zhichao was arrested for inquiry; Song Qing took over command of the armies and sent Shicheng to guard Hushan.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Zhichao was arrested and brought to trial. Song Qing took command of the forces and sent Shicheng to hold Hushan.

sentences.zh: 未幾，銘軍潰，諸軍皆走，士成猶悉力以御。

translations.literal: Before long the Ming Army broke; all armies fled, yet Shicheng still exerted his full strength to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Liu Mingchuan's force collapsed and the other units fled, but Shicheng still fought with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 日軍大集，力不支，退扼大高嶺。

translations.literal: The Japanese army massed in great numbers; unable to sustain the effort, he withdrew to hold Dagao Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Japanese forces massed in overwhelming numbers. Unable to hold, he fell back to defend Dagao Ridge.

sentences.zh: 是時遼西危棘，士成請奇兵出敵後截其運道，諸帥不從，乃自率師偪雪裡站而陣。

translations.literal: At that time western Liaoning was critically perilous; Shicheng requested a surprise force to strike behind the enemy and cut their supply route; the commanders did not follow, so he himself led his army to press Xuelizhan and form battle lines.
translations.idiomatic: Western Liaoning was in grave peril. Shicheng proposed sending a flanking force to cut the enemy's supply lines, but the other commanders refused. He then led his troops forward to confront the Japanese at Xuelizhan.

sentences.zh: 除夕，置酒飲將士，預設伏以待，日軍果來襲，大敗之分水嶺，斬日將富剛三造。

translations.literal: On New Year's Eve he set out wine for officers and soldiers, pre-positioned ambushes to wait, the Japanese army indeed came to attack, and he inflicted a great defeat at Fenshuiling, beheading the Japanese general Tomonaga Sanzo.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Eve he feasted his officers, laid ambushes, and when the Japanese attacked as expected routed them at Fenshuiling, killing the Japanese general Tomonaga Sanzo.

sentences.zh: 優詔褒勉，授直隸提督。

translations.literal: A generous edict praised and encouraged him, and he was appointed Zhili provincial commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: An edict commended him warmly and appointed him provincial military governor of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 和議成，還駐蘆臺。

translations.literal: When peace was concluded, he returned to garrison at Lutai.
translations.idiomatic: After peace was concluded he returned to garrison Lutai.

sentences.zh: 北洋創立武衛軍，改所部三十營為前軍，與宋慶、董福祥、袁世凱並為統帥。

translations.literal: The Northern Seas established the Wuwei Army; his thirty battalions were reorganized as the Front Army, and he, together with Song Qing, Dong Fuxiang, and Yuan Shikai, were made commanders-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: The Beiyang command created the Wuwei Army, reorganizing his thirty battalions as the Front Army; he served as one of its four commanders alongside Song Qing, Dong Fuxiang, and Yuan Shikai.

sentences.zh: 慶、福祥用舊法訓練，世凱軍仿日式，士成軍則半仿德式，是為武衛四軍。

translations.literal: Qing and Fuxiang used old methods of training; Shikai's army imitated the Japanese style; Shicheng's army was half modeled on the German style—these were the four Wuwei armies.
translations.idiomatic: Song and Dong trained their men by traditional methods, Yuan's troops followed Japanese drill, and Shicheng's forces were partly trained on the German model—these were the four Wuwei armies.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，拳匪亂，戕總兵楊福同，命士成相機剿辦。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the Boxer bandits rebelled and killed Regional Commander Yang Futong; Shicheng was ordered to suppress them as circumstances permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In 1900 the Boxers rose in revolt and killed Regional Commander Yang Futong. Shicheng was ordered to suppress them as circumstances allowed.

sentences.zh: 匪焚黃村、廊坊鐵軌，士成阻止之，弗應，擊殺數十人。

translations.literal: The bandits burned the Huangcun and Langfang railway tracks; Shicheng tried to stop them, they did not heed, and he killed several tens of men.
translations.idiomatic: When the Boxers burned the railway at Huangcun and Langfang, Shicheng tried to stop them. They refused, and he killed several dozen of them.

sentences.zh: 其黨大恨，訴諸朝，朝旨訶責士成。

translations.literal: Their faction hated this greatly and appealed to the court; an imperial edict rebuked Shicheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Boxers were furious and appealed to the court, which issued an edict rebuking Shicheng.

sentences.zh: 時匪麕集天津可二萬，遇武衛軍輒詬辱，士成檢勒部下毋妄動。

translations.literal: At the time bandits gathered in Tianjin to about twenty thousand; encountering the Wuwei Army they always reviled and insulted them; Shicheng strictly restrained his subordinates not to act rashly.
translations.idiomatic: Some twenty thousand Boxers had gathered in Tianjin and abused Wuwei troops whenever they met them. Shicheng strictly forbade his men to retaliate.

sentences.zh: 榮祿慮激變，馳書慰解之，士成覆書曰：「匪害民，必至害國！

translations.literal: Ronglu feared provoking a sudden change and sent a hurried letter to console and mediate; Shicheng replied: "The bandits harm the people and will surely come to harm the state!"
translations.idiomatic: Ronglu, fearing a wider explosion, wrote urging restraint. Shicheng replied, "The Boxers harm the people and will surely harm the state!"

sentences.zh: 身為提督，境有匪不能剿，如職何？

translations.literal: As a provincial commander-in-chief, if within my jurisdiction there are bandits I cannot suppress, what of my office?
translations.idiomatic: As a provincial commander, how can I hold my post if bandits run riot in my jurisdiction and I do nothing?

sentences.zh: 」乃鬱鬱駐楊村觀變。

translations.literal: He then gloomily garrisoned at Yangcun and watched how events developed.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew in frustration to Yangcun to watch events unfold.

sentences.zh: 會英、法諸國聯軍至，士成三分其軍，一護鐵路，一留蘆臺，而自率兵守天津。

translations.literal: When the allied armies of Britain, France, and other nations arrived, Shicheng divided his army in three: one part guarded the railway, one remained at Lutai, and he himself led troops to defend Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: When the allied armies of Britain, France, and other powers arrived, Shicheng divided his force in three: one detachment guarded the railway, one remained at Lutai, and he personally led the rest to defend Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 連奪陳家溝、跑馬廠、八里台，徑攻紫竹林，喋血八晝夜，敵來益眾，燃毒煙砲，我軍稍卻。

translations.literal: He successively seized Chenjiagou, Paomachang, and Balitai, pressed straight to attack Zizhulin, fought bloodily for eight days and nights, the enemy came in ever greater numbers, fired poison-smoke cannon, and our army slightly withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Chenjiagou, Paomachang, and Balitai in succession and pressed the attack on the Zizhulin concessions. For eight days and nights the fighting raged; as enemy reinforcements poured in and poison-gas shells were fired, his troops were forced to give ground.

sentences.zh: 士成立橋上手刃退卒，顧諸將曰：「此吾致命之所也，逾此一步非夫矣！

translations.literal: Shicheng stood on the bridge and personally killed retreating soldiers; turning to the generals he said: "This is where I shall give my life; to cross one step beyond is not the act of a man!"
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng stood on the bridge and personally cut down fleeing soldiers. Turning to his officers he said, "Here I will die. Any man who retreats one step further is no soldier of mine!"

sentences.zh: 」遂殞於陣，腸胃洞流。

translations.literal: He then fell in battle, his entrails streaming through a gaping wound.
translations.idiomatic: He fell in battle, his body torn open.

sentences.zh: 詔賜卹。

translations.literal: An edict granted mourning stipends.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted mourning stipends.

sentences.zh: 閱二載，以世凱言，贈太子少保，諡忠節，建專祠。

translations.literal: After two years, on Shikai's recommendation, he was posthumously granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, given posthumous title Zhongjie, and a dedicated shrine was built.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later, on Yuan Shikai's recommendation, he was posthumously granted the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, honored with the posthumous name Zhongjie, and a shrine was erected in his memory.

sentences.zh: 羅榮光，湖南乾州人。

translations.literal: Luo Rongguang was a native of Qianzhou in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Rongguang came from Qianzhou in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 初隸曾國籓麾下，補把總。

translations.literal: At first he served under Zeng Guofan and was appointed platoon commander.
translations.idiomatic: He first served under Zeng Guofan and was appointed platoon commander.

sentences.zh: 同治初，李鴻章規三吳，從西將華爾克青浦，攻南橋鎮、柘林，直搗其巢，大敗之。

translations.literal: In the early Tongzhi period Li Hongzhang planned for the three Wu regions; following the Western general Ward from Qingpu, he attacked Nanqiao Town and Zhelin, struck straight at their nest, and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Tongzhi era, when Li Hongzhang campaigned in the lower Yangtze, Rongguang followed the Western officer Ward from Qingpu, attacked Nanqiao and Zhelin, stormed the rebel stronghold, and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 乘勝复沙川、金山，遷守備。

translations.literal: Pressing the victory, he recovered Shachuan and Jinshan and was transferred to garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: Following up the victory he recovered Shachuan and Jinshan and was promoted to garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 又從西將戈登釋常、昭圍，以次下太倉、崑山諸邑。

translations.literal: He again followed the Western general Gordon in lifting the sieges of Changshu and Zhaoqing, and in succession reduced Taicang, Kunshan, and other districts.
translations.idiomatic: He then served under Gordon in relieving the sieges of Changshu and Zhaoqing and in succession captured Taicang, Kunshan, and other towns.

sentences.zh: 累擢參將。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to colonel.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted repeatedly until he reached the rank of colonel.

sentences.zh: 攻常州，先登，城复，遷副將，賜號果勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In attacking Changzhou he was first to scale the wall; when the city was recovered he was transferred to deputy commander and granted the title Guoyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: At the assault on Changzhou he was first over the wall. After the city was recovered he was made deputy commander and granted the title Guoyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 除狼山鎮右營游擊。

translations.literal: He was appointed battalion commander of the right camp of Langshan Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed battalion commander of the right camp at Langshan Garrison.

sentences.zh: 蘇軍分援浙、皖、閩，連克湖州、長興、廣德、漳州、漳浦諸城，與有功，擢總兵。

translations.literal: The Jiangsu Army was sent in separate relief to Zhejiang, Anhui, and Fujian, successively capturing Huzhou, Changxing, Guangde, Zhangzhou, Zhangpu, and other cities; he shared in the merit and was promoted to regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangsu forces were dispatched to aid Zhejiang, Anhui, and Fujian, capturing in succession Huzhou, Changxing, Guangde, Zhangzhou, Zhangpu, and other cities. For his part in these victories he was promoted to regional commander.

sentences.zh: 六年，東捻擾魯疆，榮光以偏師游弋淮南北，敗捻於運。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the eastern Nian harassed Shandong; Rongguang with a detached force ranged north and south of the Huai and defeated the Nian on the Grand Canal.
translations.idiomatic: In 1867, when the eastern Nian raided Shandong, Rongguang led a detached column along the Huai and defeated them on the Grand Canal.

sentences.zh: 東捻回竄江、淮，分寇海、沭、邳、宿，並擊退之。

translations.literal: The eastern Nian doubled back into the Yangtze and Huai regions, raiding in separate bands Hai, Shuyang, Pi, and Su; he beat them back in every case.
translations.idiomatic: When the eastern Nian doubled back into the Yangtze and Huai regions and raided Hai, Shuyang, Pi, and Su, he drove them off in every engagement.

sentences.zh: 明年，西捻窺滑、濬，我師躡之，榮光戰數挫，而勇氣彌厲。

translations.literal: The next year the western Nian probed Hua and Jun; our army pursued them; Rongguang suffered several defeats in battle, yet his courage grew still fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when the western Nian threatened Hua and Jun, Rongguang pursued them. Though he suffered several setbacks, his fighting spirit only grew fiercer.

sentences.zh: 鴻章謀困之黃、運間，緣河築長壘，榮光壁當敵衝，相持凡三閱月。

translations.literal: Hongzhang planned to trap them between the Yellow River and the Grand Canal, building a long rampart along the river; Rongguang walled himself against the enemy's main thrust and held for three months in all.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang planned to trap them between the Yellow River and the Grand Canal and built a long defensive line along the waterway. Rongguang held the point of main enemy pressure for three full months.

sentences.zh: 會霖雨，寇多陷淖死，榮光復躡之東北，勢益蹙，張總愚自沉於河。

translations.literal: When heavy rains came, many rebels sank in the mire and died; Rongguang again pursued them northeast; their situation grew still tighter, and Zhang Zongyu drowned himself in the river.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rains came, and many rebels drowned in the mud. Rongguang pressed the pursuit northeast; the rebels' situation tightened, and Zhang Zongyu drowned himself in the river.

sentences.zh: 事寧，晉記名提督。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, he was promoted to titular provincial commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign ended he was promoted to titular provincial military governor.

sentences.zh: 自是徙防金陵、武昌、西安，凡二年。

translations.literal: From then on he was transferred to garrison Nanjing, Wuchang, and Xi'an for two years in all.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred in turn to garrison Nanjing, Wuchang, and Xi'an over a period of two years.

sentences.zh: 移駐天津，補大沽協副將。

translations.literal: He moved to garrison Tianjin and was appointed deputy commander of the Dagu cooperative garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted to Tianjin and appointed deputy commander of the Dagu garrison.

sentences.zh: 光緒七年，創設水雷營，遴各營將士演習，兼授化電測量諸學。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Guangxu he established a naval mine battalion, selected officers and soldiers from each camp for drill, and also taught chemistry, electricity, surveying, and related studies.
translations.idiomatic: In 1881 he established a naval mine battalion, selected officers and men from every unit for training, and also taught chemistry, electricity, surveying, and related subjects.

sentences.zh: 既而北塘、山海關相繼設，皆受成於榮光。

translations.literal: Before long Beitang and Shanhaiguan were set up in succession, all taking their model from Rongguang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon similar units were established at Beitang and Shanhaiguan, all following the model Rongguang had created.

sentences.zh: 醇親王閱北洋軍，以其教練有方，薦授天津鎮總兵。

translations.literal: When Prince Chun reviewed the Beiyang Army, because his training was effective he was recommended and appointed regional commander of Tianjin Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Chun inspected the Beiyang forces and found Rongguang's training exemplary, he recommended him for appointment as commander of the Tianjin garrison.

sentences.zh: 位漸顯，服食儉約若老兵然。

translations.literal: As his position gradually grew prominent, his food and clothing remained frugal like an old soldier's.
translations.idiomatic: Though his rank rose steadily, he lived as frugally as a common veteran.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，擢喀什噶爾提督，未之官而拳亂起，八國兵艦入寇，榮光守大沽砲台。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was promoted to Kashgar provincial commander-in-chief; before taking office the Boxer turmoil arose, warships of the eight powers invaded, and Rongguang defended the Dagu forts.
translations.idiomatic: In 1900 he was promoted to military governor of Kashgar, but before he could take up the post the Boxer uprising broke out and the fleets of the eight powers invaded. Rongguang remained to defend the Dagu forts.

sentences.zh: 大沽水深廣，河道縈曲，曲有台，備險奧，外兵懾其勢，弗敢進。

translations.literal: Dagu's waters were deep and broad, the channels winding; at each bend stood a fort, prepared in hidden strength; foreign troops feared its power and did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: The waters at Dagu were deep and wide, the channels winding, with a fort at every bend—formidable defenses that kept foreign fleets at bay.

sentences.zh: 榮光備益嚴，乃佯就款，使人言於裕祿，謂第得四五艘入口護僑商，無他意，裕祿許之。

translations.literal: Rongguang's preparations grew still stricter; the enemy then pretended to negotiate and sent word to Yulu that they sought only four or five ships to enter and protect foreign merchants, with no other intent; Yulu permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Rongguang tightened his defenses still further. The enemy then feigned negotiation, telling Yulu through intermediaries that they sought only four or five ships to enter and protect foreign merchants. Yulu consented.

sentences.zh: 榮光聞而大驚，力阻，而敵艦已踵入，將及台，遽出砲仰擊。

translations.literal: On hearing this Rongguang was greatly alarmed and strove to block it, but enemy ships had already followed in close; as they neared the forts he suddenly brought out cannon and fired upward at them.
translations.idiomatic: Rongguang was appalled and tried desperately to stop them, but enemy vessels had already followed in. As they neared the forts he opened fire.

sentences.zh: 榮光再謁裕祿乞發戰令，諜者已報台毀，榮光憤極，歸，拔刀殺眷屬，曰：「毋令辱外人手！

translations.literal: Rongguang again called on Yulu begging for a battle order; spies had already reported the forts destroyed; Rongguang was furious beyond measure; returning home, he drew his sword and killed his family, saying: "Do not let them fall into foreigners' hands!"
translations.idiomatic: Rongguang again begged Yulu for orders to fight, but spies had already reported the forts destroyed. In a fury he returned home, drew his sword, and killed his family, saying, "They shall not be dishonored by foreigners!"

sentences.zh: 」遂出赴難，一僕隨之，不知所終。

translations.literal: He then went out to meet the crisis; one servant followed him, and nothing more was known of their end.
translations.idiomatic: He then went out to face the enemy, one servant following him; neither was seen again.

sentences.zh: 他日得其屍台下，僕屍亦在焉。

translations.literal: Another day his corpse was found below the fort, and the servant's corpse was there as well.
translations.idiomatic: Later his body was found below the fort, the servant's corpse beside it.

sentences.zh: 沒三日而天津陷，時年六十有七。

translations.literal: Within three days of his death Tianjin fell; he was then sixty-seven years old.
translations.idiomatic: Three days after his death Tianjin fell. He was sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 壽山，字眉峰，袁氏，漢軍正白旗人，黑龍江駐防，吉林將軍富明阿子。

translations.literal: Shou Shan, styled Meifeng, of the Yuan clan, a Hanjun bannerman of the Plain White Banner garrisoned in Heilongjiang, was the son of Jilin General Fuming'a.
translations.idiomatic: Shou Shan, whose style was Meifeng, was a Hanjun bannerman of the Plain White Banner stationed in Heilongjiang and the son of Jilin General Fuming'a.

sentences.zh: 以父任為員外郎，兼襲騎都尉世職，遷郎中。

translations.literal: Through his father's office he became a vice director, also inherited the hereditary office of commandant of cavalry, and was transferred to director.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father's position he became a vice director in the Board of Revenue, inherited the hereditary rank of commandant of cavalry, and was later promoted to director.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十年，日軍犯奉天，自請赴前敵，充步隊統領。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Guangxu the Japanese army invaded Fengtian; he volunteered to go to the front and served as infantry commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1894, when Japanese forces invaded Fengtian, he volunteered for the front and was appointed commander of the infantry.

sentences.zh: 弟永山領馬隊，數與日軍戰，复草河嶺，克連山關，進薄鳳凰城。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yongshan led the cavalry, fought the Japanese army several times, recovered Caoheling, captured Lianshanguan, and pressed close to Fengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yongshan commanded the cavalry, fought the Japanese repeatedly, recovered Caoheling, took Lianshanguan, and advanced to the outskirts of Fengcheng.

sentences.zh: 敵援至，永山歿於陣，壽山被重創。

translations.literal: When enemy reinforcements arrived, Yongshan fell in battle and Shou Shan received grave wounds.
translations.idiomatic: When enemy reinforcements arrived, Yongshan was killed in battle and Shou Shan was severely wounded.

sentences.zh: 以敢戰，兼領鎮邊軍馬隊。

translations.literal: For his daring in battle, he was also put in charge of the Frontier Defense Army cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: For his valor he was also given command of the Frontier Defense Army cavalry.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，降敕褒嘉。

translations.literal: After a year an imperial edict descended commending him.
translations.idiomatic: A year later the throne issued an edict commending him.

sentences.zh: 官軍既克海城，壽山領七十騎詣遼南诇敵勢，遇之湯岡子，搏戰，槍彈入右腹，貫左臀出，戰愈猛，敵稍卻，馳還壁，血縷縷滿衣袴。

translations.literal: After government troops had taken Haicheng, Shou Shan led seventy horsemen south into Liaodong to scout the enemy; they met at Tangangzi and fought hand to hand; a bullet entered his right abdomen and passed out through his left hip; he fought still more fiercely; the enemy slightly withdrew; he galloped back to camp, blood streaming down his clothes and trousers.
translations.idiomatic: After government forces captured Haicheng, Shou Shan led seventy horsemen into southern Liaodong to reconnoiter the enemy. At Tangangzi they clashed in close combat. A bullet entered his right abdomen and exited through his left hip, yet he fought all the harder until the enemy gave ground. He galloped back to camp with blood soaking his garments.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其勇，遷知府，賞花翎。

translations.literal: The throne praised his courage, transferred him to prefect, and rewarded him with the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised his courage, promoted him to prefect, and awarded him the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，調充鎮邊軍左路統領，徙駐黑龍江城。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was transferred to serve as commander of the left wing of the Frontier Defense Army and moved his garrison to Heilongjiang City.
translations.idiomatic: In 1897 he was appointed commander of the left wing of the Frontier Defense Army and moved his headquarters to Heilongjiang City.

sentences.zh: 越二年，除知開封遺缺知府，未之官，值東北邊防亟，超改黑龍江副都統。

translations.literal: After two years he was appointed to the vacant prefecture of Kaifeng but did not take office; as the northeastern frontier was urgent, he was promoted beyond normal procedure to Heilongjiang deputy lieutenant-general.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he was appointed prefect of Kaifeng but never took up the post. With the northeastern frontier in crisis he was promoted out of turn to deputy lieutenant-general of Heilongjiang.

sentences.zh: 明年春，入覲，垂詢邊情甚悉，命佐將軍恩澤治軍。

translations.literal: The next spring he had audience; the throne inquired minutely about border conditions and ordered him to assist General Enze in managing the army.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring he had audience with the throne, which questioned him closely on border affairs and ordered him to assist General Enze in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 疏請增募十五營，調諳邊事者十餘人，躬詣上海購軍械，自長崎、海參崴、伯利循海歸，潛度形勢，備戰守。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting to raise fifteen additional battalions, transferred more than ten men versed in border affairs, personally went to Shanghai to purchase arms, returned by sea from Nagasaki, Vladivostok, and Khabarovsk, secretly surveyed the terrain, and prepared for war and defense.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to raise fifteen new battalions and transferred more than ten men experienced in frontier affairs. He went personally to Shanghai to buy arms, returned by sea via Nagasaki, Vladivostok, and Khabarovsk, surveyed conditions covertly, and prepared for war.

sentences.zh: 新軍成，而恩澤卒於任，朝命代之。

translations.literal: When the new army was formed, Enze died in office and the court ordered Shou Shan to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When the new army was ready, Enze died in office and the court appointed Shou Shan to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 既蒞事，鏟姦弊，明賞罰，圖要塞；

translations.literal: Once he took charge, he rooted out corruption, clarified rewards and punishments, and mapped strategic passes;
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he rooted out corruption, enforced discipline in rewards and punishments, and surveyed strategic strongpoints;

sentences.zh: 手訂行陣操法，頒之各將領，使番上，授以方略；

translations.literal: he personally drafted field drill regulations, issued them to each commander, had them rotate attendance, and taught them strategy;
translations.idiomatic: he personally drafted field regulations, distributed them to all commanders, required them to attend in rotation, and instructed them in strategy;

sentences.zh: 雖末弁亦接見，籍記備器使。

translations.literal: even junior lieutenants were received in audience, registered, and assigned equipment for use.
translations.idiomatic: and even junior lieutenants were received, registered, and assigned their equipment.

sentences.zh: 二十六年夏，拳亂作，俄軍數千聲為保護哈爾濱鐵軌，紛集海蘭泡，乞假道。

translations.literal: In the summer of the twenty-sixth year the Boxer turmoil arose; several thousand Russian troops, claiming to protect the Harbin railway, gathered at Hailanpao and begged passage.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of 1900 the Boxer uprising broke out. Several thousand Russian troops, claiming to protect the Harbin railway, massed at Blagoveshchensk and asked permission to pass through.

sentences.zh: 壽山曰：「敵偪我都，我假敵道，如大義何！

translations.literal: Shou Shan said: "The enemy presses on our capital region; if we grant the enemy passage, what of righteousness!"
translations.idiomatic: Shou Shan said, "The enemy threatens our territory. If we grant them passage, what becomes of our duty?"

sentences.zh: 」拒之。

translations.literal: He refused them.
translations.idiomatic: He refused.

sentences.zh: 遂檄愛琿副都統鳳翔禦北路，呼倫貝爾副都統依興阿禦西路，通肯副都統慶祺禦東路，令各嚴戒備毋浪戰；

translations.literal: He then issued orders to Aihui Deputy Lieutenant-General Feng Xiang to defend the northern route, Hulunbuir Deputy Lieutenant-General Yixing'a the western route, and Tongken Deputy Lieutenant-General Qingqi the eastern route, commanding each to maintain strict readiness and not fight rashly;
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Aihui Deputy Lieutenant-General Feng Xiang to hold the northern route, Hulunbuir Deputy Lieutenant-General Yixing'a the west, and Tongken Deputy Lieutenant-General Qingqi the east, instructing each to maintain strict readiness and avoid reckless engagements;

sentences.zh: 並牒俄勿進兵，願負保路責。

translations.literal: and also sent a dispatch to Russia not to advance troops, offering to bear responsibility for protecting the railway.
translations.idiomatic: and sent word to the Russians not to advance, pledging to take full responsibility for protecting the railway.

sentences.zh: 而俄軍已分道進，重以鐵路土工可十餘萬索值，倡罷工，揚言與俄為難。

translations.literal: But the Russian army had already advanced by separate routes; moreover some hundred thousand railway laborers demanded back pay, called strikes, and openly declared hostility to Russia.
translations.idiomatic: But Russian forces had already advanced along several routes. Meanwhile some hundred thousand railway laborers demanded back pay, went on strike, and openly threatened Russia.

sentences.zh: 壽山亟下令軍中曰：「保鐵路，護難民，全睦誼，違者殺無赦！

translations.literal: Shou Shan urgently ordered the army: "Protect the railway, guard refugees, preserve friendly relations—violators shall be killed without pardon!"
translations.idiomatic: Shou Shan urgently ordered his troops: "Protect the railway, safeguard refugees, preserve good relations—violators will be executed without mercy!"

sentences.zh: 」復使統領吉祥約富拉爾基監工蓋爾肖甫入城，俾釋疑懼，而蓋爾肖甫乃擊殺工人宵遁。

translations.literal: He also had Commander Jixiang invite the Fularji overseer Giershoff into the city to ease suspicion and fear, but Giershoff instead attacked and killed workers and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: He also had Commander Jixiang invite the railway overseer Giershoff at Fularji into the city to ease tensions, but Giershoff attacked and killed workers and fled by night instead.

sentences.zh: 壽山猶強為容忍也，慎導俄民出境，籍錄其財物備還，然俄軍不為止，入寇愛琿及黑河屯，華人被迫赴水者，屍蔽江下。

translations.literal: Shou Shan still forced himself to tolerate this, carefully guiding Russian civilians out of the territory and recording their property for return, yet the Russian army did not stop, invaded Aihui and Heihe Tun, and Chinese forced into the water left corpses covering the river downstream.
translations.idiomatic: Shou Shan still strove to restrain his men, carefully escorting Russian civilians out of the territory and recording their property for return. Yet Russian forces did not halt, invaded Aihui and Heihe, and Chinese driven into the river left the waters downstream strewn with corpses.

sentences.zh: 三姓、呼倫貝爾又紛紛告警，壽山亟電吉林將軍長順會攻哈爾濱，然猶囑其語俄總監工，謂若罷兵，願以全家質。

translations.literal: Sanxing and Hulunbuir again sent repeated alarms; Shou Shan urgently telegraphed Jilin General Changshun to join in attacking Harbin, yet still instructed him to tell the Russian chief engineer that if they ceased hostilities he would pledge his whole family as guarantee.
translations.idiomatic: Alarms poured in from Sanxing and Hulunbuir. Shou Shan telegraphed Jilin General Changshun to join in attacking Harbin, yet still told him to inform the Russian chief engineer that if Russia halted hostilities he would stake his entire family as guarantee.

sentences.zh: 當是時，諸路軍皆潰敗，北路統領崇玉，營官德春、瑞昌，西路統領保全，東路營官保林，並陷陣死，於是俄遂偪齊齊哈爾省城。

translations.literal: At that time armies on every route were broken; Northern Route Commander Chongyu, battalion officers Dechun and Ruichang, Western Route Commander Baoquan, and Eastern Route battalion officer Baolin all fell in battle; thereupon Russia pressed on Qiqihar provincial city.
translations.idiomatic: By then every route had collapsed. Northern commander Chongyu, battalion officers Dechun and Ruichang, western commander Baoquan, and eastern battalion officer Baolin all died in battle, and Russian forces pressed on Qiqihar.

sentences.zh: 既而聞聯軍媾和，乃遣同知程德全往商和議，而自守「軍覆則死」之義，命妻及子婦先裁，手繕遺疏，猶惓惓於墾政，並致書俄將領囑勿戕民。

translations.literal: Soon hearing the allied armies had made peace, he sent Subprefect Cheng Dequan to negotiate peace, while himself upholding the principle that "if the army is destroyed, the commander dies"; he ordered his wife and daughters-in-law to kill themselves first, wrote his final memorial by hand, still earnestly concerned with land reclamation policy, and also wrote Russian generals urging them not to harm the people.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that the allied powers had made peace, he sent Subprefect Cheng Dequan to negotiate, while he himself upheld the principle that a commander must die with his defeated army. He ordered his wife and daughters-in-law to kill themselves first, wrote his final memorial by hand—still earnestly concerned with land reclamation—and wrote to Russian commanders begging them not to harm civilians.

sentences.zh: 閱日，具衣冠，飲金，臥柩中，不死；

translations.literal: The next day, dressed in full regalia, he drank gold and lay in his coffin, yet did not die;
translations.idiomatic: The next day, dressed in full official regalia, he took poison and lay in his coffin, yet did not die.

sentences.zh: 呼其屬下材官擊以槍，不忍，手顫機動，彈出中左脅，猶不死；

translations.literal: he called his subordinate arms officer to shoot him; the man could not bear it; his hand trembled, the trigger moved, the bullet flew out and struck the left ribs, yet he still did not die;
translations.idiomatic: He called his arms officer to shoot him. The man could not bear to do it; his hand shook, the gun fired, and the bullet struck Shou Shan's left ribs—yet he still lived.

sentences.zh: 更呼材官擊小腹，仍不死；

translations.literal: he called again for the arms officer to shoot his lower abdomen, and still did not die;
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the man to shoot again at his lower abdomen. Still he did not die.

sentences.zh: 呼益厲，又擊之，氣始絕。

translations.literal: he called still more fiercely, and after another shot his breath finally ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He shouted still more fiercely; after another shot his breath finally ceased.

sentences.zh: 先是詔責其開邊釁，部議奪職。

translations.literal: Earlier an edict had rebuked him for provoking a border conflict, and the ministry deliberated stripping his office.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier an edict had blamed him for provoking the border conflict, and the Board recommended stripping his rank.

sentences.zh: 後以總督徐世昌請復官，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職，附祀富明阿祠。

translations.literal: Later, on Governor-General Xu Shichang's request, his office was restored; he was granted the hereditary offices of commandant of cavalry and commandant of light cavalry, and given collateral sacrifice in Fuming'a's shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at Governor-General Xu Shichang's request, his rank was restored and hereditary offices granted; he was given collateral sacrifice in Fuming'a's shrine.

sentences.zh: 族孫瑞昌，充北路營官，俄陷黑河，與統領崇玉同戰歿。

translations.literal: His clan grandson Ruichang served as Northern Route battalion officer; when Russia took Heihe he fell in battle together with Commander Chongyu.
translations.idiomatic: His clansman Ruichang served as battalion officer on the northern route; when the Russians took Heihe he fell in battle alongside Commander Chongyu.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔，字集庭，漢軍鑲黃旗人，吉林駐防。

translations.literal: Feng Xiang, styled Jiting, was a Hanjun bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner garrisoned in Jilin.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Xiang, whose style was Jiting, was a Hanjun bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner stationed in Jilin.

sentences.zh: 累官協領。

translations.literal: He rose through repeated offices to battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十一年，中日事起，將軍長順赴奉督師，鳳翔任餽運，給食不乏。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Guangxu, when the Sino-Japanese affair arose, General Changshun went to Fengtian to command the army; Feng Xiang was put in charge of supply transport and provisions never ran short.
translations.idiomatic: In 1895, when war broke out with Japan, General Changshun went to Fengtian to command the army. Feng Xiang handled supply transport and never let provisions run short.

sentences.zh: 尋擢愛琿副都統。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Aihui deputy lieutenant-general.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to deputy lieutenant-general of Aihui.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，俄將固畢乃脫爾來假道，壽山令愛琿戒備。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the Russian general Gribsky came requesting passage; Shou Shan ordered Aihui to prepare defenses.
translations.idiomatic: In 1900 the Russian general Gribsky came requesting passage. Shou Shan ordered Aihui to prepare its defenses.

sentences.zh: 俄軍已自黑龍江下駛，翼日，俄官廓米薩爾名闊利士密德者，浮軍艦至，鳳翔遣軍拒之三道溝。

translations.literal: Russian troops had already sailed down the Amur; the next day the Russian officer Komissar named Kolchitsky came with warships; Feng Xiang sent troops to resist him at Sandaogou.
translations.idiomatic: Russian troops had already sailed down the Amur. The next day the Russian officer Kolchitsky arrived with warships, and Feng Xiang sent troops to block him at Sandaogou.

sentences.zh: 闊利士密德來謁，申前請，弗允，赬怒去，令舟師擊我，而我師已先發，殲其軍官二，闊利士密德被重創，奔還海蘭泡，旋卒。

translations.literal: Kolchitsky came to call and renewed his former request; it was not granted; he left flushed with anger and ordered his fleet to attack us, but our army had already opened fire first, destroyed two of their officers, Kolchitsky was gravely wounded, fled back to Hailanpao, and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Kolchitsky came to negotiate and renewed his request for passage. When refused he left in a fury and ordered his fleet to attack, but Chinese forces had already opened fire, killing two Russian officers. Kolchitsky was gravely wounded, fled back to Blagoveshchensk, and soon died.

sentences.zh: 於是黑河軍與海蘭泡俄軍相轟擊者數日。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Heihe army and the Hailanpao Russian army exchanged bombardment for several days.
translations.idiomatic: For several days the Heihe garrison and Russian forces at Blagoveshchensk exchanged fire.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔令統領王仲良率騎旅三百渡江擊之，始小挫，繼獲大勝。

translations.literal: Feng Xiang ordered Commander Wang Zhongliang to lead three hundred cavalry across the river to attack them; at first they suffered a small setback, then won a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Xiang ordered Commander Wang Zhongliang to lead three hundred cavalry across the river to attack. After an initial setback they won a major victory.

sentences.zh: 俄軍緣江遁，師往馳之，會其軍艦泊江岸，載歸。

translations.literal: Russian troops fled along the river; our army pursued them and happened upon their warships moored on the bank and brought them back.
translations.idiomatic: Russian forces fled along the river. Pursuing troops came upon their warships moored on the bank and captured them.

sentences.zh: 閱二日，又渡江來，擊卻之。

translations.literal: After two days they crossed the river again; our forces beat them back.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later they crossed again and were driven back.

sentences.zh: 遲明，又率步旅六千自五道河濟，右路統領崇玉望見之，其軍皆樹我幟，衣我衣，意為漠河護礦兵也，弗敢擊，既登岸始覺，而勢已不可遏，我師敗績，崇玉殞於陣，愛琿陷。

translations.literal: At daybreak they again led six thousand infantry across from Wudaohe; Southern Route Commander Chongyu saw them; their army all flew our banners and wore our uniforms; he thought them Mohe mine-guard troops and did not dare attack; only after they landed did he realize, but the momentum could no longer be stopped; our army was defeated, Chongyu fell in battle, and Aihui fell.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn six thousand Russian infantry crossed from Wudaohe. Commander Chongyu saw them flying Chinese banners and wearing Chinese uniforms and mistook them for mine-guard troops from Mohe, daring not to fire. Only after they landed did he realize his error, but by then it was too late. Chinese forces were routed, Chongyu was killed, and Aihui fell.

sentences.zh: 壽山聞之，亟令鳳翔回援，弗及。

translations.literal: When Shou Shan heard this he urgently ordered Feng Xiang to return to reinforce, but it was too late.
translations.idiomatic: Shou Shan urgently ordered Feng Xiang to return and reinforce Aihui, but it was too late.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔駐兜溝子，去愛琿七十里。

translations.literal: Feng Xiang garrisoned Dougouzi, seventy li from Aihui.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Xiang withdrew to Dougouzi, seventy li from Aihui.

sentences.zh: 踰月，俄軍復至，槍彈雨下，鳳翔以戰為守，相持累日。

translations.literal: After a month Russian troops came again, bullets falling like rain; Feng Xiang used battle as defense and held for many days.
translations.idiomatic: A month later Russian forces returned, bullets falling like rain. Feng Xiang fought to hold his ground and the two sides grappled for days.

sentences.zh: 黑龍江行軍故無棚帳，戰罷露宿，眾苦寒，以是軍有怨聲，鳳翔慮譁潰，復以地勢平衍難扼守，乃請壽山結陣徐退，抵內興安嶺軍焉，去兜溝子又百六十里。

translations.literal: Heilongjiang campaigns traditionally had no tents; after battle they slept in the open; the troops suffered bitter cold, and for this the army murmured; Feng Xiang feared mutiny and rout; moreover the terrain was level and hard to defend; he therefore asked Shou Shan to form ranks and withdraw slowly, reaching the Inner Xing'an Range encampment, another one hundred sixty li from Dougouzi.
translations.idiomatic: Heilongjiang troops had no tents on campaign and slept in the open after battle. The bitter cold bred discontent, and Feng Xiang feared mutiny. The terrain was also too open to defend. He asked Shou Shan for permission to withdraw in good order to the Inner Xing'an Range, another hundred sixty li from Dougouzi.

sentences.zh: 未幾，俄軍爭上嶺，勢洶洶，師失利，仍扼嶺拒之。

translations.literal: Before long Russian troops vied to ascend the ridge in surging force; our army suffered defeat but still held the ridge to block them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Russian forces pressed up the ridge in overwhelming numbers. Chinese troops were driven back but still held the heights to block them.

sentences.zh: 敵攻益亟，鳳翔悉甲出，令曰：「有後者斬！

translations.literal: As enemy attacks grew fiercer, Feng Xiang sent out his full armor and ordered: "Whoever falls back shall be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: As the enemy pressed harder, Feng Xiang committed his full force and ordered, "Any man who retreats will be beheaded!"

sentences.zh: 」而自赴前敵督懾。

translations.literal: He himself went to the front line to supervise and overawe.
translations.idiomatic: He himself went to the front to command.

sentences.zh: 有材官稍卻，立使飛騎斬之。

translations.literal: When an arms officer slightly fell back, he immediately sent a mounted courier to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: When one officer began to fall back, he immediately sent a mounted courier to cut him down.

sentences.zh: 材官懼，大呼陷陣，俄軍少卻，復進，遂大敗，署北路翼長恆玉斷一臂，俄將卒死傷無算。

translations.literal: The arms officers feared this, shouted and charged the line; Russian troops slightly withdrew, then advanced again; our side won a great defeat; Acting Northern Route wing commander Hengyu lost an arm; Russian officers and soldiers died and were wounded beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, the officers shouted and charged. The Russians gave ground, then pressed forward again, and Chinese forces won a crushing victory. Acting northern wing commander Hengyu lost an arm; Russian casualties were beyond count.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔戰既酣，右臂左足兩受彈傷，墜馬者三，輒复躍上，鏖戰不少休，既還，嘔血數升而死。

translations.literal: Feng Xiang fought with utmost intensity; his right arm and left foot both received bullet wounds; he fell from his horse three times and each time leaped back on; he battled without pause; after returning he vomited several sheng of blood and died.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Xiang fought with ferocious intensity. His right arm and left foot were both shot; three times he fell from his horse and three times leaped back into the saddle. He fought without rest. After returning to camp he vomited blood and died.

sentences.zh: 事聞，優恤如製。

translations.literal: When news arrived, generous mourning stipends were granted according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, generous mourning stipends were granted according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 崇玉，通肯正藍旗佐領。

translations.literal: Chongyu was a company commander of the Plain Blue Banner at Tongken.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyu was a company commander of the Plain Blue Banner at Tongken.

sentences.zh: 時同死事者，玉慶，黑龍江城世管佐領。

translations.literal: At the same time others who died in the affair included Yuqing, hereditary company commander of Heilongjiang City.
translations.idiomatic: Others who died in the fighting included Yuqing, hereditary company commander of Heilongjiang City.

sentences.zh: 城陷被執，詈不絕口，死最慘。

translations.literal: When the city fell he was seized and reviled without cease; his death was the most wretched.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he was captured, cursed his captors without cease, and died a most terrible death.

sentences.zh: 扎魯布，黑龍江城水師四品官。

translations.literal: Zhalubu was a fourth-rank officer of the Heilongjiang naval force.
translations.idiomatic: Zhalubu was a fourth-rank officer of the Heilongjiang naval force.

sentences.zh: 懷印以殉，死後猶手握印不可脫。

translations.literal: He clasped his seal to die with it; after death he still gripped the seal and it could not be removed.
translations.idiomatic: He died clutching his official seal; after death his grip could not be loosened.

sentences.zh: 又段國英，宜黃人，以縣丞榷鹽阿什河。

translations.literal: Also Duan Guoying, a native of Yihuang, served as assistant magistrate collecting salt tax at the Ashi River.
translations.idiomatic: Also Duan Guoying of Yihuang, who as assistant magistrate collected the salt tax at the Ashi River.

sentences.zh: 俄兵至，令讓所處屯兵，嚴詞拒之，縛而去；

translations.literal: When Russian troops arrived they ordered him to yield his station and garrison troops; he refused in stern words and was bound and taken away;
translations.idiomatic: When Russian troops arrived they ordered him to yield his post. He refused in the strongest terms and was bound and taken away.

sentences.zh: 旋釋歸，則俄兵已佔其地，且懸俄幟，國英大哭曰：「中國亡矣！

translations.literal: soon released and returned, he found Russian troops had already occupied his ground and raised the Russian flag; Guoying wept loudly: "China is destroyed!"
translations.idiomatic: Soon released, he found Russian troops had occupied his station and raised the Russian flag. Guoying wept aloud, "China is lost!"

sentences.zh: 」觸石，頭裂，死。

translations.literal: He struck a stone; his head split, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: He dashed his head against a stone and died.

sentences.zh: 俄人觀者皆嘆息。

translations.literal: Russian onlookers all sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Even the Russian onlookers sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 論曰：秉衡清忠自矢，受命危難，大節凜然，此不能以成敗論也。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Bingheng pledged himself to integrity and loyalty, accepted command in peril, and his great integrity stood austere—this cannot be judged by success or failure.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: Bingheng devoted himself to integrity and loyalty, accepted command in a time of peril, and upheld his principles with unwavering dignity—qualities that cannot be measured by success or failure alone.

sentences.zh: 聯軍之佔津、海也，長驅而入，唯士成阻之；

translations.literal: When the allied armies occupied Tianjin and the coast, they drove straight in; only Shicheng blocked them;
translations.idiomatic: When the allied armies seized Tianjin and the coast they swept inland unopposed—only Shicheng stood in their way;

sentences.zh: 俄兵之侵龍江也，乘隙以進，唯壽山拒之：固知必不能敵，誓以一死報耳。

translations.literal: When Russian troops invaded the Amur region, they advanced by seizing openings; only Shou Shan resisted them: he surely knew he could not prevail, yet vowed to repay with a single death.
translations.idiomatic: When Russian forces invaded the Amur, they pressed forward wherever they found an opening—only Shou Shan stood in their way. He knew he could not win, yet swore to repay the state with his life.

sentences.zh: 榮光爭大沽，鳳翔守愛琿，雖已無救於大局，而至死不屈，外人亦為之奪氣，何其壯哉！

translations.literal: Rongguang fought for Dagu, Feng Xiang defended Aihui; though they could no longer save the overall situation, they refused to yield unto death, and foreigners too were struck with awe—how magnificent!
translations.idiomatic: Rongguang held Dagu, Feng Xiang defended Aihui. Though neither could alter the outcome of the war, both fought to the death without yielding, and even the foreigners were awed by their courage. How magnificent they were!
